Detect slow oscillations

Source: R/compute_slow_oscillations.R
compute_slow_oscillations.Rd

Detects slow oscillations (slow waves) in an EEG channel with the algorithm of yasa.sw_detect() in YASA (Vallat & Walker, 2021; YASA 0.8.1), and reproduces its output: the same events, at the same sample positions, with the same amplitudes (see Details).

Usage

compute_slow_oscillations(
  psg,
  channel = NULL,
  stages = NULL,
  freq_so = c(0.3, 1.5),
  amp_ptp_threshold_uv = c(75, 350),
  duration_pos_s = c(0.1, 1),
  duration_neg_s = c(0.3, 1.5),
  amp_neg_uv = c(40, 200),
  amp_pos_uv = c(10, 150),
  transition_hz = 0.2
)

Arguments

psg

An mrpheus_psg object from prepare_psg().

channel

Character. EEG channel label. If NULL (default), the first non-bad EEG channel is used.

stages

Integer vector or NULL. Epoch indices in which peaks are accepted (for example the N2 and N3 epochs). If NULL, all epochs are used. As in YASA, only the peaks have to lie in these epochs: an event can start or end outside them.

freq_so

Numeric vector of length 2. Band-pass of the slow oscillation band (Hz), as YASA's freq_sw. Default c(0.3, 1.5).

amp_ptp_threshold_uv

Numeric vector of length 2. Minimum and maximum peak-to-peak amplitude (uV), exclusive. Default c(75, 350).

duration_pos_s

Numeric vector of length 2. Minimum and maximum duration of the positive phase (s), exclusive. Default c(0.1, 1.0).

duration_neg_s

Numeric vector of length 2. Minimum and maximum duration of the negative phase (s), exclusive. Default c(0.3, 1.5).

amp_neg_uv

Numeric vector of length 2, or NULL. Minimum and maximum absolute amplitude of the negative peak (uV), inclusive. Default c(40, 200). NULL applies no limit.

amp_pos_uv

Numeric vector of length 2, or NULL. Minimum and maximum amplitude of the positive peak (uV), inclusive. Default c(10, 150). NULL applies no limit.

transition_hz

Numeric. Width of both transition bands of the FIR filter (Hz). The -6 dB points lie half a transition band outside freq_so (0.2 and 1.6 Hz for the defaults). Default 0.2, as in YASA.

Value

A tibble with one row per detected slow oscillation:

epoch

Integer. Epoch of the negative peak.

start_s

Numeric. Onset (s) relative to the start of epoch. Can be negative, or the offset can exceed the epoch length, when the event crosses an epoch boundary.

end_s

Numeric. Offset (s) relative to the start of epoch.

duration_s

Numeric. Duration of the slow oscillation (s).

neg_peak_uv

Numeric. Value of the negative peak in the filtered signal (uV, negative).

pos_peak_uv

Numeric. Value of the positive peak (uV).

ptp_uv

Numeric. Peak-to-peak amplitude (uV).

channel

Character.

neg_peak_s

Numeric. Time of the negative peak (s from the start of the first epoch).

mid_crossing_s

Numeric. Time of the zero crossing between the negative and the positive peak (s from the start of the first epoch).

pos_peak_s

Numeric. Time of the positive peak (s from the start of the first epoch).

slope_uv_s

Numeric. Slope between the negative peak and the mid crossing (uV/s).

Details

The channel is band-passed with an FIR filter (Hamming window, zero phase, as mne.filter.filter_data()), applied to the continuous signal, not epoch by epoch. Local minima and maxima of the filtered signal are found (negative peaks with a trough between amp_neg_uv, positive peaks between amp_pos_uv) and kept if they lie in the epochs given by stages. Each negative peak is paired with the closest following positive peak, the peak-to-peak amplitude must lie within amp_ptp_threshold_uv, and the durations of the negative and positive phases (taken from the zero crossings around each peak) must lie within duration_neg_s and duration_pos_s. Every event that shares its start, and then every event that shares its end, with another event is dropped, as in YASA, so two negative peaks paired with the same positive peak are both discarded.

Amplitudes must be in uV. As YASA, the channel is skipped (with a warning) when the standard deviation of its central 90 % of samples is outside 0.1-1000 uV, which usually means a wrong unit.

The result was compared with yasa.sw_detect() on the Sleep-EDF night SC4001E0 (8.8 h at 100 Hz, and a 6.5 h version at 256 Hz) with a stage mask that cuts through events: the numbers of events are equal (2,236 and 1,000), the event times are identical, and amplitudes agree to about 1e-12 uV. The test suite checks the same agreement against stored YASA output on a synthetic EEG at 100 and 256 Hz, and on a crafted signal that reaches the edge cases of YASA's rules (tests/testthat/test-yasa-slow-oscillation-parity.R).

Not implemented: YASA's slow oscillation - spindle coupling and its remove_outliers option. Where YASA's code has quirks they are reproduced: a peak before the first zero crossing takes the last zero crossing of the recording as its previous crossing (the event is then rejected by the duration criteria).

References

Vallat, R., & Walker, M. P. (2021). An open-source, high-performance tool for automated sleep staging. eLife, 10, e70092. doi:10.7554/eLife.70092
